summary: Enlarged the Moapa River (Paiute) Indian Reservation in Nevada by adding certain described lands.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission six more months, past September 2, 1903, to finish judging American citizens' claims against Spain under the 1898 treaty.
Allowed Julia W. Wellborn to be permanently appointed a clerk in the Geological Survey without a civil-service examination.
Amended the civil-service rules to drop the exception from examination for one clerk at each pension agency who stood in for the agent during absence or disability.
Restored to settlement a half-section in the former Cheyenne and Arapahoe lands of Oklahoma Territory once held for Day County's county seat, which had moved to the town of Grand in 1893.
Let consulting engineer Allen Hazen stay on through construction and early operation of the Washington filtration plant, for no more than 24 months.
Allowed Dr. William A. White to fill the vacant superintendent's post at the Government Hospital for the Insane without a civil-service examination.
Waived the six-month service requirement so W. E. Lackland could transfer from the Treasury Department to the post office at Prescott, Arizona.
Approved reinstating Emma J. Rawlings, a former expert money teller and daughter of a Civil War veteran, to the Treasury Department post her mother had held.
Set up about sixteen military reservations across the Philippines in a single order, including Camp Stotsenberg at Angeles, Camp McGrath at Batangas, Fort San Pedro at Cebu and Warwick Barracks.
Created the Pocatello Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Laid out the rules for U.S. passports: only the Secretary of State issues them, only those owing allegiance qualify, and applicants must file a sworn, attested application with personal details.
Set aside the abandoned Camp McDowell Military Reservation in Maricopa County, Arizona Territory, for the Mojaves and other Indians living there.
Established the Siassi Military Reservation in Moro Province, Philippines, as a right of way for a pipe line.
Allowed Clarence A. Cook to be appointed a special agent of the Bureau of Corporations at $2,000 a year without a civil-service examination.
Turned the former Crow Creek Forest Reserve in Albany County, Wyoming, into the Fort D. A. Russell Target and Maneuver Reservation.

places.name: Fort D. A. Russell Target and Maneuver Reservation

summary: Established the Fort San Pedro Military Reservation at Iloilo on the island of Panay in the Philippines.
Created a 535.63-acre military reservation at Baguio in Benguet Province, Luzon, in the Philippines.
Called both houses of Congress into extraordinary session on November 9, 1903, to decide whether to approve the reciprocal trade convention with Cuba signed at Havana.
Allowed Lillian B. Kellogg to return as a piece sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Created the Aquarius Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Named Thursday, November 26, 1903, a national day of thanksgiving, asking Americans to set aside their usual work and give thanks in their homes and places of worship.
Allowed Mrs. Roy L. Quackenbush, a temporary Post-Office Department clerk, to be made permanent without examination.
Enlarged the Payson Forest Reserve in Utah, first established in 1901, to take in additional described lands.
Modified the June 30, 1903, order setting aside military and lighthouse lands in Puerto Rico.
Extended U.S. copyright protection to citizens of Cuba after assurances that Cuban law gives Americans copyright on the same basis as its own citizens.
Further modified the June 30, 1903, order setting aside military and lighthouse lands in Puerto Rico.
Allowed Francis L. Hawes of New York to be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations at $1,600 a year without examination.
Barred consular officers from using official letterheads and signatures on private correspondence.
Reserved all land on Kiska Island, Little Kiska Island and nearby islets in Alaska for naval purposes.
Created the Highwood Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Trimmed the Red Bank Military Reservation in New Jersey by handing a 400-square-foot monument site to the Interior Department.
Combined the Pine Mountain and Zaca Lake and the Santa Ynez forest reserves, plus added lands, into a single new Santa Barbara Forest Reserve in California.

places.name: Pine Mountain and Zaca Lake Forest Reserve

summary: Took over the former Republic of Hawaii's lighthouses, nearby land, buoys, beacons and records for the United States, placing them under the Light-House Board of the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Allowed Mrs. Frank L. Harrigan to return as a ruling machine feeder at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Shrank the Fort Liscum Military Reservation at Port Valdez, Alaska, to 659.89 acres.
Allowed Evelyn M. Ford to be reinstated as a clerk in the office of the Secretary of War despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Granted the abandoned Fort Marcy Military Reservation, about 17¾ acres, to the town of Santa Fe, New Mexico, which had agreed to hand it to the Board of Education to support public schools.
Allowed Mrs. G. W. Shipman to be appointed a clerk in the Office of the First Assistant Postmaster-General without examination.
Allowed Elizabeth C. Peters to return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Established the Guantánamo Bay Military Reservation in Cuba.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission another six months, past March 2, 1904, to finish judging American citizens' claims against Spain.
Transferred the Fort Yates Military Reservation in North Dakota to the Interior Department for use by the Indian Service.
Abolished the Oklahoma (City) land district, moving its lands, business and records to the Guthrie district and land office.
Further reduced the Fort Egbert Military Reservation in Alaska.
Shrank the Pine Ridge Sioux Indian Reservation by returning to the public domain the Nebraska lands added to it in January 1882.
Approved E. W. Libbey's July 1903 appointment as telegraph and telephone operator in the Department of Commerce and Labor and let him stay without examination.
Allowed Kate L. Croggan to return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Authorized the Secretary of Commerce and Labor to lease certain Alaskan islands for raising foxes.
Created the Baker City Forest Reserve in Oregon, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Let James M. Cooper and Ralston Williams work for the Army medical board studying typhoid fever in the 1898 military camps until its report was done.
Revoked the July 3, 1902, special rule that let former employees of the U.S. military government of Cuba move into matching classified-service jobs.
Allowed Matthew J. McCarty to transfer without examination to deputy surveyor and inspector at the customs port of Syracuse, New York.
Declared U.S. neutrality in the war between Japan and Russia, warning Americans against aiding either side and laying out rules on belligerent vessels, contraband and neutral rights at sea.
Established a 1,159-acre military reservation at Parang in Mindanao, Philippines.
Allowed Marie L. Baldwin, on the Minnesota clerk register, to be certified as a $900 clerk in the Office of Indian Affairs, setting aside Rule VII.
Added all commissioners of the national military parks to the War Department positions exempt from civil-service examination.
Closed all federal offices in Ohio during the funeral of Senator Marcus A. Hanna on February 19, 1904, as a mark of respect.
Amended a January 1904 order to permanently reserve the section holding the irrigation ditch and school pasture of the Pine Ridge Boarding School in Nebraska.
Allowed Francis Walker of Massachusetts to be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations at $2,000 a year without examination.
Brought nearly every War Department civil-service job in the Philippines under the classified civil service, except laborers and presidential appointees, and set terms for retaining current workers.
Allowed Merrit O. Chance to move from clerk to the Secretary of War to superintendent of post-office supplies without a noncompetitive examination.
Created the Cave Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Created the Slim Buttes Forest Reserve in South Dakota, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Corrected and reissued the grant of the abandoned Fort Marcy Military Reservation to the town of Santa Fe, New Mexico, for public use in support of its public schools.
Directed all civil, military and naval officials to observe the neutrality proclamation in the Russia–Japan war and avoid any act or speech that could irritate either combatant.
Reduced the Manila Bay Military Reservations in the Philippines, first set aside in April 1902.
Redefined the Mariveles Military Reservation in Bataan Province, Luzon, Philippines.
Shifted the boundary between the Boise and Lewiston land districts in Idaho, effective May 2, 1904.
Established the Sangley Point Military Reservation, about two acres inside the naval reservation on Cañacao Bay, Luzon, Philippines.
Widened a civil-service exception so contract physicians anywhere in the Indian service, not just at Indian schools, earning up to $720 a year could keep a private practice.
Set the pay for members of the Isthmian Canal Commission.
Returned 120 acres once reserved for the Fort Sill Indian boarding school to the public domain so the adjoining city of Lawton, Oklahoma Territory, could claim it for a park.
Opened to disposal the 160-acre St. John's Mission School tract near the Cheyenne River Agency in South Dakota after the missionary society gave up its use.
Enlarged the Fish Lake Forest Reserve in Utah, established in 1899, by redrawing its boundaries to take in more land.
Reserved tracts in Idaho's Hailey land district for future townsites along a proposed railroad through lands to be irrigated under the Reclamation Act.
Redrew the boundaries of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve in Wyoming and Montana, starting from the edge of Yellowstone National Park, and set a date for opening lands left outside to settlement.
Created the Grantsville Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Opened about 382,000 acres of Rosebud Reservation land in Gregory County, South Dakota, ceded by the Sioux, to settlement, while holding back tracts for a sub-issue station, day school and missions.
Redrew the boundaries of the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve in Colorado and set a date for opening lands left outside to settlement.
Allowed Katherine C. Masterson to be reinstated at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Further redrew the boundaries of the White River Forest Reserve in Colorado and set a date for opening lands left outside to settlement.
Created the Salt Lake Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving timbered public lands within set boundaries from settlement.
Allowed I. B. Conklin to be hired as a clerk at $3.28 a day in the paymaster's office of the Washington Navy Yard without examination.

Opened about 88,000 acres of the Devils Lake Reservation in North Dakota, including the old Fort Totten Military Reserve, ceded by Sisseton, Wahpeton and Cut-Head Sioux, to homestead and townsite entry.
Moved certain North Dakota lands from the Grand Forks land district to the Devils Lake land district, effective August 1, 1904.
Changed the civil-service rules so a person reinstated at a lower grade can be promoted back to the former grade without examination.
Cut described lands in Idaho out of the Bitter Root Forest Reserve and restored them to the public domain, with a set date for opening them to settlement.
Made an exception to the civil-service rules so Samuel D. Amen could be appointed an internal-revenue agent.
Established two Philippine military reservations: about 96.6 acres at Pasay in Rizal Province and about 131 acres at Zamboanga (Pettit Barracks) on Mindanao.
Enlarged the Fort Niobrara Military Reservation in Cherry County, Nebraska, by 25,900 acres, to about 60,000 acres.
Allowed Dr. William L. Ralph to be appointed curator of birds' eggs at the National Museum, at $100 a month, without examination.
Allowed Clarence Reeder to be appointed private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey without examination.
Let Edna K. Hoyt, a temporary State Department clerk, be made permanent at $1,200 a year without examination, at Secretary Hay's request.
Reserved about 11.7 acres at Fort Santiago in Manila, Philippines, for an ordnance depot.
